- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.00) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.67) and model is trending upward, check for mean reversion; if price hasn’t moved >5% from 10-day avg, cap forecast at 10% below recent high.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.67–1.00) and model is flat or rising, model often underestimates volatility; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 5–7 days.
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with sentiment trend.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong divergence from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with 18-day MA unless sentiment strongly contradicts it.
